name: ogeon Connector
author: ogeon

sections.description:
ogeon is an SEO and AI-search agent that writes articles for your business and publishes them to your website.

You need an ogeon account to use this plugin. It does nothing until you connect it from ogeon.

Most sites don’t need this plugin: ogeon connects through WordPress’s own Application Passwords with one click. Some hosts and security plugins block that approval page or switch Application Passwords off. This plugin is the alternative for those sites.

What it does:

  • Makes a random connection key when you activate it. You copy it from Settings → ogeon into ogeon.
  • Adds REST API routes under ogeon/v1 that only answer to that key: to check the connection, publish an article, fill in your SEO plugin’s fields, and save your site’s llms.txt.
  • Publishing the same article again updates the same post instead of making a copy, also when a slow connection makes ogeon send it twice at the same moment.
  • If another post already uses the article’s address (slug), or a page does on sites whose addresses are just the post name, the article is saved as a draft so you can look first.
  • Fills in the meta description and focus keyword for Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO or SEOPress, and the meta description for The SEO Framework, when one of them is active. Fields you wrote yourself in WordPress are kept when ogeon updates an article.
  • Adds the article’s FAQ structured data (FAQPage JSON-LD) to the post’s page, when the article has a FAQ.
  • Downloads the article’s featured image into your media library, also from image links that don’t end in .jpg or .png.
  • Shows AI assistants such as ChatGPT and Perplexity a short summary of your site at /llms.txt (see llmstxt.org). ogeon writes it when you click “Fix it for me” in its GEO Pack; WordPress answers the address, so no file is written to your server. A real llms.txt file in your site’s root folder always wins. You can switch this off.
  • Tells IndexNow search engines (Bing, Yandex and others) about each article as soon as it is published, and again when you click “Ask search engines again” in ogeon. You can switch this off.
  • When you click “Fix it for me” in ogeon’s GEO Pack, writes your homepage’s meta description and replaces a free contact email with the one on your own domain. Each change is shown to you in ogeon before it is made.
  • When you click “Update now” in ogeon, updates this plugin (and only this plugin) to the newest version on wordpress.org, using WordPress’s own updater. You can also turn WordPress’s automatic updates on or off for this plugin from ogeon. Nothing is updated without your click.
  • Shows the update notice for this plugin on your Plugins screen as soon as a new version is on wordpress.org. To do that it reads this plugin’s public page on wordpress.org (api.wordpress.org) at most every six hours, only in the admin area or WordPress’s scheduled tasks; nothing about your site is sent.
  • Shows on Settings → ogeon whether ogeon has connected and which article it published last.
  • Credits each post to the author you choose. Posts are only attributed to that person: ogeon never signs in as them or as any other user.
  • Article HTML is filtered with WordPress’s own allowed-HTML rules for posts.

If a security plugin turns the REST API off for visitors who are not logged in, this plugin lets requests through for its own ogeon/v1 routes only, and only when they carry the key. Every other route keeps your security settings. Blocks made by your web server itself (outside WordPress) can’t be lifted by a plugin; ask your host to allow /wp-json/ogeon/v1/ or ?rest_route=/ogeon/v1/.

External services

This plugin works with two outside services.

ogeon (the service this plugin connects to)

  • What it is used for: ogeon sends your site the articles it wrote for you, and checks the connection.
  • What is sent and when: the plugin does not send anything to ogeon on its own. ogeon calls the plugin’s ogeon/v1 routes on your site when you connect, each time it publishes, when you ask it to fix your llms.txt (it then sends the llms.txt text it wrote for your site), when you approve a GEO Pack fix for your homepage description or contact email (it then sends the description, or the old and new email addresses), and when you click Update now or the automatic updates switch in ogeon. Its connection check also returns whether automatic updates are on for this plugin and whether a newer version is available. The new version itself is downloaded from wordpress.org, as with any plugin update. In its answers the plugin returns the site name, address, WordPress and plugin version, the chosen author’s name, which SEO plugin is active, your post categories, and the address of each post it creates.
  • When ogeon publishes an article with a featured image, the plugin downloads that image from the address ogeon sends (ogeon’s image storage, on supabase.co).
  • Terms of service: https://sites.google.com/view/ogeon/terms-of-service
  • Privacy policy: https://sites.google.com/view/ogeon/privacy-policy

IndexNow (run by Microsoft Bing, Yandex, Seznam.cz and other search engines)

  • What it is used for: telling search engines that a new or updated article exists, so they can visit it sooner.
  • What is sent and when: each time ogeon publishes or updates an article, and when you click “Ask search engines again” for an article in ogeon, the plugin sends that article’s address, your site’s host name and a public IndexNow key to https://api.indexnow.org/indexnow, which shares it with the participating search engines. Nothing about your visitors is sent. The plugin also answers requests for the key at /{key}.txt so search engines can check it.
  • It is on by default. You can switch it off in Settings → ogeon, and it is skipped while your site asks search engines not to index it (Settings → Reading).
  • Terms of service (the Privacy section covers data): https://www.indexnow.org/terms
  • About IndexNow: https://www.indexnow.org/
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin in Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin and activate it.
  2. Open Settings → ogeon and copy the connection key.
  3. In ogeon go to Settings → Publishing → WordPress, open Connect with the ogeon plugin, paste your site address and the key, and click Connect.
sections.faq:
Do I need this plugin?

Only if the one-click “Connect with WordPress” in ogeon doesn’t work on your site, for example because the approval page shows “Gone” or “Forbidden”.

Is the key safe?

The key is 64 random characters, made on your server. Anyone who has it can publish posts on your site, so keep it private. You can make a new one in Settings → ogeon at any time; the old one stops working right away.

What can ogeon do on my site with the key?

Only create posts and update the posts it created, with their featured image, categories and SEO fields. The key can’t sign in, manage users, plugins or themes, or change settings.

What happens when I deactivate or delete the plugin?

ogeon can no longer publish. Deleting the plugin removes the key and its settings. Posts that ogeon already published stay.
sections.changelog:
1.9.7

  • The cover the plugin puts at the top of a post’s text loads first, so the page shows its main image sooner.

1.9.6

  • Updating a post from ogeon keeps it a draft, pending, private or scheduled when you took it off your site by hand.
  • Updating a post keeps the cover at the top of its text, built from the post’s featured image with its size, so WordPress adds the smaller sizes.

1.9.5

  • Deleting the plugin also removes the version information it saved from wordpress.org.

1.9.4

  • WordPress shows “There is a new version of ogeon Connector available” on the Plugins screen as soon as a new version is on wordpress.org. For a few hours after a release, wordpress.org’s update check could still say the old version was the newest. The new version still comes from wordpress.org.

1.9.3

  • When automatic updates are turned off on your site, ogeon now tells you what turned them off (for example your host’s Installatron or Softaculous) and where to turn them on.

1.9.2

  • “Update now” in ogeon works right after a release too. For a few hours after a new version comes out, WordPress may not see it yet; the plugin then takes the new version from its wordpress.org page instead, still the same wordpress.org download.

1.9.1

  • Fixes the “Keep the ogeon plugin updated” switch in ogeon, which said automatic updates were turned off on every site.

1.9.0

  • Update this plugin from ogeon with one click, and turn WordPress’s automatic updates on or off for it from ogeon. Updates always come from wordpress.org through WordPress’s own updater, and only when you click in ogeon.

1.8.0

  • GEO Pack in ogeon can now write your homepage’s meta description into your SEO plugin, also when your homepage lists your latest posts.
  • GEO Pack can replace a free contact email (such as Gmail) with the one on your own domain in your pages, page builder content (Elementor and others), menus, widgets and theme settings. Your WordPress admin email is never changed.

1.7.1

  • Fixes publishing on WordPress sites that run on SQLite (for example WordPress Studio or WordPress Playground). Since 1.6.0 every article there was refused with “This article is already being published”.

1.7.0

  • “Ask search engines again” in ogeon sends an article to IndexNow on demand and shows the search engines’ answer, including whether they can read your site’s IndexNow key.

1.6.1

  • Settings → ogeon no longer says The SEO Framework gets a focus keyword. That plugin has no focus keyword field; ogeon fills in its meta description.

1.6.0

  • All in One SEO 4 now shows the meta description and focus keyword ogeon sends. They are written to All in One SEO’s own table, not only to post meta.
  • Yoast SEO shows a new description at once, instead of after the post is next saved by hand.
  • Adds SEOPress (description and focus keyword) and The SEO Framework (description).
  • An article whose address matches an existing page is saved as a draft when post addresses are just the post name, so it never hides behind the page.
  • Two calls for the same article at the same moment, for example a retry on a slow host, no longer make two posts.
  • Publishing keeps running on slow hosts after ogeon stops waiting, so a retry finds the finished post.
  • A very long article that the server cannot filter is refused with a clear error instead of being saved empty.
  • Emoji in the meta description no longer stop it from saving on older databases.

1.5.0

  • Layered and Timeline articles from ogeon get their reading buttons: readers pick the short answer, the full guide or the stage they are in. The plugin loads a small stylesheet and script only on posts that have them.

1.4.1

  • After switching from an Application Password, ogeon can update the posts it published before the switch and send their SEO fields, instead of making a new draft.

1.4.0

  • A site already connected to ogeon with an Application Password can switch to this plugin in one click: ogeon reads the connection key for you. Only a WordPress administrator can read it.

1.3.0

  • Serves the llms.txt that ogeon writes for your site at /llms.txt, so “Fix it for me” in ogeon’s GEO Pack works on sites connected with this plugin. Switch it off in Settings → ogeon.
  • New icon and banner with Ogi, ogeon’s agent.

1.2.0

  • ogeon can send the meta description and focus keyword to your SEO plugin when you ask it to.
  • Updating an article no longer replaces SEO fields you wrote yourself in WordPress.

1.1.0

  • A cover regenerated in ogeon replaces the featured image when the article is updated. Covers set by hand are still kept otherwise.
  • An update whose address is taken by another page keeps the post live at its current address.

1.0.0

  • First release: connection key, verify and publish routes, Yoast / Rank Math / All in One SEO fields, featured images, author setting, IndexNow, connection status.
